sessionTitle: Discovering Power App Data with M365 Copilot using MCP

announcements.name: Power Apps MCP is in public preview
announcements.shortDescription: Available now through the preview Maker portal so developers can expose app data to M365 Copilot.
announcements.longDescription: The Power Apps MCP is currently in public preview, allowing developers to expose their Power App data for agentic and Microsoft 365 Copilot discovery. The session explains Power Platform as a suite of tools that enables business subject matter experts and pro developers to build mission-critical applications, automate and standardize processes, analyze app-captured data, and create AI-driven solutions over connected data without deep technical skills. Attendees are pointed to links to set up their own Power Apps and make data exposable in M365.

announcements.name: Enabling the MCP yields four standard CRUD tools
announcements.shortDescription: Turning on the Copilot MCP setting automatically provides create, read/review, edit/update, and query tools against the app's Dataverse data.
announcements.longDescription: In the preview Maker portal (previewmake.preview.powerapps.com [inferred]), developers go into their app settings, turn on Copilot control, and then enable the Copilot MCP via a yes/no setting. When turned on, the app's MCP automatically provides four basic CRUD tools—edit, create, review, and query—against the app's data. These standard tools appear in the MCP alongside any custom tools, and the same MCP is surfaced in Microsoft 365.

announcements.name: Custom MCP tools with targeted Dataverse fields
announcements.shortDescription: Developers can build custom tools that pass specific selected fields (rather than whole tables) to produce focused data insights at a prompt.
announcements.longDescription: Beyond the basic CRUD experience, developers can create custom tools for the MCP to deliver richer data insights at a prompt for their users. The presenter demonstrates custom tools such as 'show equipment work order status' that produce tailored UI like cards and charts—dashboard-style experiences similar to what one would build in Power Platform—showing equipment, inspections, and statuses at a glance. These custom tools let users view, edit, and modify live application data without leaving their context.

announcements.name: Fluent UI generation via Claude/GitHub Copilot skill
announcements.shortDescription: Microsoft provides a Power Platform skill for Claude and GitHub Copilot that turns a tool's JSON structure into a Fluent UI HTML file, with local preview against sample data.
announcements.longDescription: When a custom tool is tested, the Maker portal generates a JSON structure of the selected fields and table data. Microsoft provides a Power Platform skill for Claude and GitHub Copilot (used via the Power Platform plug-in in VS Code) that turns this JSON into a Fluent UI HTML file. The developer simply types 'generate MCP APP UI' in Claude, supplies a description and the JSON, and it produces the HTML; alternatively developers fluent in Fluent UI can hand-code their own. In the demo a robust timeline UI took about two to three minutes to generate.

announcements.name: Declarative agent packaging for M365
announcements.shortDescription: Each set of tools can be downloaded as a declarative agent zip file and uploaded into Microsoft 365 (e.g., Teams) for end users.
announcements.longDescription: After adding tools and pasting in the Fluent UI, the developer saves and publishes the MCP, then uses the download option to package the tools as a declarative agent zip file. This download must be repeated each time a new tool is created. The resulting zip lands in the Downloads folder and is uploaded into Microsoft 365—for example via Teams by choosing manage apps and uploading the app—though doing so requires appropriate M365 or Global Admin permissions.
